channel.title: Pier & Point · Hearst Tower
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Hearst Tower (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Hearst Tower: Hearst Tower's page now says its 2009 date is when a newspaper reported the complex open, not an opening date, and it lists conflicting architect and resident-capacity figures instead of choosing one.

item.title: Correction · Hearst Tower: The four UCSF Block 20 housing buildings showed an October 2005 opening that was only ever a 2002 forecast. Their completion now rests on SFGate's May 2009 report that the campus had four residential buildings, so they were complete by then; the actual opening date is still not confirmed.

item.title: Correction · Hearst Tower: Hearst Tower's 431 apartments and address 1560 3rd St were removed: the Regents item gives 430 apartment-style units for all four buildings together, and no readable source gives a per-tower count or that address. The record no longer says the building opened around 2005 or in June 2005: no source read gives an opening date (Langan gives none and UCSF's housing page could not be read), so the milestone now carries the October 2005 full occupancy that the November 2002 Regents item anticipated, marked expected. The Regents approval is described as the committees approving and forwarding to the Board. Use now reads student, postdoctoral scholar and family housing (Langan, Regents) instead of student and faculty, the facts about the four-building complex cite Langan, the example of a parcel spanning several UCSF buildings now says about 12.2 acres at 675 Mission Bay Blvd, the SOM architect attribution cites arcCA Digest, and the aerial photo's caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'.

item.title: Added · Hearst Tower: The November 2002 UC Regents capital-improvement budget of $112,816,000 covers the whole Block 20 project (Hearst Tower plus the Housing North, Housing West and Student Housing mid-rise buildings) with no per-building breakdown, so it was never a cost for any one of them. It is now listed once in the shared site-wide cost list for Mission Bay, and all four records point to it; each already discussed the figure in its notes without treating it as its own total.

Source: UC Regents Committees on Grounds and Buildings and on Finance, joint meeting minutes, 2002-11-13 (https://regents.universityofcalifornia.edu/minutes/2002/gbf1102.pdf).

item.title: Complete · Hearst Tower: SFGate's May 31, 2009 article on the Helen Diller building says "With the opening of the Diller building at 1450 Third St., the Mission Bay campus now has four research buildings, a community center and four residential buildings." The article does not name Block 20 or this housing complex, so reading its four residential buildings as the four-building Block 20 complex is an inference. May 31, 2009 is the article's publication date, not an opening date: it shows the complex was open by then, and no source read gives the date it actually opened (the November 2002 Regents item had anticipated full occupancy by October 2005) (~2009)

item.title: Planned · Hearst Tower: UC Regents' Grounds and Buildings and Finance committees approve, and vote to present to the Board, a $112,816,000 budget and external financing for the Mission Bay Block 20 Housing and Retail Project -- one 15-story tower and three mid-rise buildings around a shared courtyard, 298,800 residential asf and 430 apartment units total -- with construction to begin June 2003 and full occupancy anticipated by October 2005 (Nov 13, 2002)
